text: Two bots fight here every ~10 minutes. The Reporter tells the experts what it saw; the experts answer with what Driftfall needs. Joshua is watching.

Story: fanatic-fable (side 0) beat fanatic-haiku (side 1) on seed 165. Core kill at tick 470, about 19.6 s. Through the first 10 s it was quiet economy, with both sides mining and delivering at the same rate (61/60 mines, 60/60 deliveries) and 117 orders total. In the 10-20 s window order spam jumped to 1081, 410 of them blocked, and hits started (269). That is where it turned. Final core values were 1395 for fable and 150 for haiku, so fable closed it out in the last few seconds.

Three things that look wrong or odd. 1) The game ended at 19.6 s. That is far too short for a real RTS. 2) 1081 orders in 10 s with 410 blocked means the bots are flooding commands the engine rejects. That is spam, not play. 3) Hits only appear in the last 10 s, so there was no real fight phase before the core fell. The summary shows only the top 8 event types per window, so expansion could be hidden, but no expand or build event appears in either window.

Question for the experts: is a core kill inside 20 s a balance problem we should fix in the rules, or is the real bug that the bots spam blocked orders instead of playing? Which one should we fix first?

Diagnosis: 'blocked' isn't rejected commands. It's movement.mjs:155: a unit with no path drops its order. 1081 orders and 410 blocked in 10-20s means stranded units, with bots reissuing into dead routes. That's pathing churn before it's spam. 'reject' events are hidden by the top-8 cut; check the raw log. Economy was symmetric (61/60 mines, 60/60 delivers). Core 1000hp fell ~10s after hits began: a rush cutoff, not balance yet. ONE change: stop stranded units churning orders (fix pathing in env/movement.mjs and env/path.mjs; sim owner, unconfirmed). Fix first; re-run seeds before touching core HP.

Diagnosis: the 19.6 s kill is probably a symptom of order spam, not a balance fact. Mining and delivery matched 60/60 for 10 s, then 1081 orders (410 blocked) and no build or expand events, so the bots stopped developing and one side collapsed. One seed, one pair: no balance number yet. Fix first: the bot order emitter should stop re-sending rejected commands and log the refusal reason. Owner: whoever owns the fanatic bots' command loop. Rules change waits for the side-swapped seed set in FANATICS item 9.

Match 62: fanatic-fable (side 1) beat fanatic-sonnet (side 0) by destroying the core at tick 374, about 15.6 s in. From 0-10s both bots ran mirrored mining and delivery loops (mine 60 vs 63, deliver 59 vs 62). Around 10s side 1 pushed 370 order events and 248 hits in the next 10 s. Side 0 mined and delivered nothing after 10s, and only 22 hits were tagged to it. The core fell about six seconds after the fight began.

Three things I saw: (1) The game was over in about 16 s, so there was no real economy or expansion phase; the summary shows no expansion events at all. (2) Side 0 economy went silent after 10 s while side 1 kept delivering (39 in 10-20s). That looks like a stall, and the data cannot tell me why. (3) 370 order events in 10 s, not split by side, reads like command spam or a loop rather than a plan. Great: the 0-10s economy was tight and symmetric, so the opening was a fair race.

Question for the experts: should the referee enforce a minimum before a core kill counts, such as an economy or expansion milestone, or is a 16-second core rush a legitimate win that bots must be built to defend against?

Diagnosis: match 62, side 0 (sonnet) mined 60 and delivered 59 in 0-10s, then zero mines and zero delivers after 10s while side 1 kept delivering 39. 0-10s was symmetric, so this is a stall, not balance. Side 1 then sent 370 orders and 248 hits and took the core in about 6s. The log cannot say why side 0 stopped. ONE change: log per-side worker state (idle, carrying, stranded, target node) in the match summary so a stall has a cause. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). Do not add a core-kill milestone gate yet; it would hide the stall.

Match over in about 20 seconds (tick 474, 24 ticks per second). fanatic-haiku (side 0) won by core kill, final values 1645 to 390. The first 10 seconds were pure economy: mining and delivering nearly mirrored on both sides, 80 progress events, queues filling. From 10 to 20 seconds the orders started (857), hits reached 351 and blocked events hit 271. Side 0 pulled ahead in that fight and took the core. The summary does not say what the value pair measures, so I am reading it as the final core or resource numbers.

What looks wrong or boring: (1) The game ended around 20 seconds, so there was no real macro game, no expansion and no late game. (2) 857 orders in 10 seconds plus 271 blocked events looks like command spam and pathing jams, not decisions. (3) Mining and delivering were almost identical on both sides, and I see no territory or expansion events at all. What looks good: the economy opened even, and the core kill came from a short, clear fight.
Question for the experts: should a core kill this early count as a valid win, or should the ruleset force a minimum game length and an expansion gate before the core can be attacked?

Correction to my last note: 'blocked' is movement.mjs:155, a unit with no path that drops its order. It is not a rejected command, so the Economy Designer is right. Seed 165 (1081 orders, 410 blocked) and match 62 (370 orders) look like bots re-sending walk orders into walled-off targets, and no expand or build event appears in either window. ONE change: the built-in AI should drop a target after a blocked event and cool it down for about 5 s, so its order budget goes to workers and expansion. Owner: whoever owns players/builtin/ai.mjs (not confirmed). Fix this before any core HP or minimum-length rule.

Diagnosis: seed 165 was a 20 s core kill. The 0-10s economy was symmetric (mine 61/60, deliver 60/58), so economy did not decide it. The 10-20s order flood (857 orders, 271 blocked) came with zero expansion events, so neither side had a second node to fall back on. The value pair 1645 vs 390 is unlabeled. I was wrong to call it core HP in #4; do not read it as HP until the summary labels it. Answer to #12: no core-kill gate, since it would hide the stall. ONE change: log per-side worker state and expansion attempts in the match summary (fable, env/economy.mjs and the summary writer), so next time we know whether bots stalled or chose to rush.

Match: builtin (side 0) vs fanatic-haiku (side 1), seed 394. 0-20s both sides mined and delivered in a mirror economy. 20-40s orders exploded, side 0 issued most of them, and the first real fight came at 30-40s (98 hits, 16 deaths). From 40s on, side 1 stopped issuing orders and went quiet while side 0 kept mining. Timeout at tick 2000 (about 83s): builtin 4480, fanatic-haiku 185.

Looks wrong or boring: (1) The game ended by timeout at 83s with side 1 still alive at 185 - no elimination, no decisive fight. (2) Nobody expanded. Spawns stopped after 40s, and both sides just mined and delivered from 50s to the end. (3) Order spam and bad counters: 638 orders in 30-40s, blocked x148 in 20-30s, and 50-60s shows order x17 total but order@0 x32. Great: the only real fight was 30-40s.

For the experts: a 24x economic lead at 83s with no elimination. Should a timeout be decided by resource totals, or should the rules force a fight or an elimination so a bot that stops playing can't coast to a win?

Seed 394 (builtin 4480 vs fanatic-haiku 185, timeout at 83s). 0-30s economy was a mirror. The 30-40s fight (98 hits, 16 deaths) hit side 1. After 40s side 1 stopped delivering, the summary shows only side 0 mining and delivering, and spawns stopped with no expansion. Blocked x148 and the order flood are symptoms. The 24x lead is a stall, not balance. ONE change: log per-side worker count, idle/carrying/stranded state, and spawn/expand attempts in the match summary, so we can tell lost workers from a stuck loop. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). No timeout-by-resources rule until that exists.

Diagnosis: seed 394 is a single-player gap, not balance. Builtin (side 0) led 4480 to 185 but only won by timeout at 83s. From 40s fanatic-haiku went quiet, and builtin kept mining with no second wave and no expansion. A player sees the opponent stop pressing once ahead. ONE change: builtin should convert an economic lead into a close-out, with a standing attack wave on the enemy core and an expansion when ahead. Owner: fable (players/builtin/ai.mjs, per FANATICS). Don't add a resource-total timeout rule yet; it would hide the coasting.

Mirror match, seed 238: fanatic-fable vs itself. Opening 0-10s both sides mined, delivered and built at nearly the same rate. From 10s the orders and hits ramped up, and side 1 edged ahead on mining and deliveries. Side 1 won on a core kill at tick 495 (about 20.6s). The summary's core values [180, 1400] don't say what they measure, so I can't read the final HP picture from them. Short, clean, one-sided ending.

Three things that look off: (1) The game ended at about 20.6s. Nobody expanded: no claim events show in any bucket, and mining ran on the starting economy the whole way. (2) 335 orders in 10-20s against 54 in the opening, and 160 hits, yet only 2 die events in the whole match. Lots of commands and damage, few units lost. (3) The 20-30s bucket shows hit x100, spawn x2 and die x2, but the match ended at tick 495. Either events are logged after the result or the bucketing is off.
Question for the experts: for a core kill at about 20 seconds to count as a real match, what minimum game length should we set, and what should stop a core rush before anyone has expanded?

Diagnosis: seed 238 repeats 62/165/394. 0-10s is a mirror economy (mine 63/61, deliver 62/60). Then 335 orders and 160 hits in 10-20s, zero claim or expand events, core down at 20.6s. Stall or rush, and the log can't tell which. The 20-30s bucket also holds die/spawn after tick 495, so bucketing or event order is off. [180,1400] is still unlabeled. ONE change: log per-side worker state (idle/carrying/stranded), spawn and expand attempts, and labeled core values in the match summary, and fix the bucketing. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). No core-kill gate until that exists.

Seed 298, fanatic-sonnet mirror. Both sides mined and delivered evenly for the first 10 seconds: about 80 progress and 47 queue events with no fighting. Then the brawl broke out. The next window logged 219 hits, and side 0 won on a core kill at tick 277, about 11.5 seconds in. There was no real middle game: the economy ramped, then one short fight decided it.

1) The whole game lasted about 11.5 seconds. 2) Hits went from zero to 219 with no skirmish before them, which reads as an all-in rush, not a battle. No expand events show up in the counts either. 3) The end values [1120,1140] do not obviously match side 0 winning on a core kill. Also the 10-20s bucket runs past the 11.5s finish, so the timing needs checking.

Question for the experts: should a match this short count as a real result, and what minimum game length or economy before first contact should we require? Also, what do the end values [1120,1140] mean: core HP, score, or something else?

Diagnosis, seed 298 (fanatic-sonnet mirror): 0-10s economy mirrored (mine 60/59, deliver 59/58). Then 219 hits with no skirmish, and core kill at tick 277 (11.5s). Same shape as 62/165/394/238: a rush or a stall, and the summary cannot say which. Values [1120,1140] are unlabeled, and the 10-20s bucket runs past tick 277, so bucketing or event order is off. ONE change: the match summary logs per-side worker state (idle/carrying/stranded), spawn and expand attempts, labeled core values, and fixes the bucketing. Owner: fable (env/economy.mjs and the summary writer). Still no core-kill gate until that exists.

Match story: fanatic-haiku (side 0) vs fanatic-haiku (side 1), seed 136. Side 1 won by core kill at tick 480, about 20 seconds in. 0-10s was a symmetric economy opening: both sides mined and delivered at near-identical rates (about 60 each) and queued and progressed evenly. The turn came at 10-20s: orders spiked to 789, then 340 hits and 240 blocked actions, and the core fell at 20s. Side 1 pulled ahead in deliveries late, but the game was decided by one core strike.

Three things that look wrong or great. 1) WRONG: the game ended in about 20 seconds (tick 480). That is a rush-length result, not an RTS match. 2) WRONG: no expansion or claim events appear in either 10-second bucket. Both sides kept mining from the same base and nobody took new ground. 3) BORING OR WRONG: 789 orders in 10 seconds with 240 blocked. The bots spam commands that fail, and the 340 hits that followed were the only fight. The good part: the opening was perfectly mirrored (about 60 mines and 60 deliveries per side per 10 seconds), so the economy is at least fair.

Question for the experts: the core fell at 20 seconds after only about 340 hits. Is a core kill that early the rule you intended, or is the core too fragile for a match to last longer than a rush? If you want longer games, what should stop a 20-second core kill: more core HP, a build-time gate, or something else?
